prerequisites: Test whether a complete model satisfies every premise.
Understand the difference between one possible model and all valid models.
explanation: A necessary conclusion is true in every model satisfying the premises. One valid drawing in which the conclusion is true is not enough. To disprove necessity, build a model that keeps every premise true but makes the conclusion false. If no model satisfies the premises, report inconsistency rather than treating every conclusion as established. Universal statements here do not assert existence.

worked.action: All L are M and all M are N force all L are N.
worked.justification: Any proposed L outside N would be an M outside N, contradicting the second premise.

worked.action: All L are M does not force all M are L. Use one object in M alone.
worked.justification: This model satisfies the premise and falsifies the converse conclusion; one counterexample is sufficient.

worked.action: Some L are M plus some M are N does not force some L are N. Use object1 in L,M and object2 in M,N.
worked.justification: Both premises have witnesses but the L/N overlap is empty. A single three-way overlap was merely one possible drawing.

worked.action: Some L are M and no M are N force some L are not N.
worked.justification: The required L/M witness cannot be in N. This combines existence with exclusion.

worked.action: All L are M alone does not force some L are M, because L can be empty.
worked.justification: Add an explicit existence premise before making an existential conclusion.

worked.action: Some L are M and no L are M have no valid model.
worked.justification: The required witness lies in a forbidden region. Distinguish inconsistent premises from a conclusion that is merely not necessary.

hint: Try to preserve every premise while falsifying the conclusion. If you claim necessity, explain why such a counterexample cannot exist.
shortcut: Propagate a required witness through universal inclusions and exclusions; for universal conclusions, trace a hypothetical violating object.
limitation: A true conclusion in one diagram establishes possibility only. These authored checks use no existential import unless a witness is explicitly stated.
